## Flowchart of iSCAT Image Processing

I have optimized the image processing pipeline for iSCAT data to speed up the filtering process and remove 
the 20 Hz vibration noise. The flowchart of the new pipeline is shown above. I have speed up the filtering 
from 20 minutes for 1000 frames down to 1 minute for 4000 frames without losing any particle signal.

## 20 Hz Vibration Noise Removal

As seen in the image above, there is a 20 Hz noise when plot the intensity for highlighted 
ROI. My strongest guess is that the 20 Hz noise is due to the mechanical vibration around the microscope. 
I have not been able to find the source of the vibration yet, but I have been able to remove the 20 Hz noise
by applying a notch filter to the FFT of the image. This noise can result in strong signal fluctuation which 
made it very hard to consistently track the particles. Previously (last week), I could track the particles 
but due to the strong signal fluctuation, one single trajectory could be broken into multiple trajectories. 

![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.10.05 (Amir Fathi - iSCAT Speedup, Vibration Filtering)\vibration-noise.png)


<!-- *╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ -->
<!-- *│ Slide                                                        │ -->
<!-- *╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ -->
## 20 Hz Vibration Noise Removal

After carefully inspecting the frequency spectrum of the ROI, I can identify the 20 Hz noise (18.5 -20.5 Hz) and 
its harmonic at 40 Hz. Carefully tuning a notch filter with a reasonable bandwidth to just remove the 20 Hz noise and its harmonic, I can remove the noise without losing any particle signal. One step further, I 
also remove the very low DC frequency (0 - 1 Hz) to remove the slow drift in the signal


![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.10.05 (Amir Fathi - iSCAT Speedup, Vibration Filtering)\temporal-notch.png)


<!-- *╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ -->
<!-- *│ Slide                                                        │ -->
<!-- *╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ -->
## 20 Hz Vibration Noise Removal

The temporal notch filter was applied after correcting the image for the uneven spatial intensity distribution.
To speed up the process and better filtering, a block of 16 by 16 pixels was used to calculate the FFT and apply the notch filter to every pixel in the block. The image above shows the result of applying the temporal notch filter to the image. The 20 Hz noise is completely removed, and the particle signal is preserved.

![](F:\Amir\OneDrive_Research\Research\Ian Liau\Weekly Reports\2026\2026.10.05 (Amir Fathi - iSCAT Speedup, Vibration Filtering)\temporal-notch-image.png)

## Tracking Results

A side by side comparison of the overlaid trajectories on the original image and the filtered image is shown above. The video of this tracking result is also attached in the report. The source images were 4313 frames
recorded at 100 fps. The recording belongs to SLB with 25% BMP at the presence of TAT. I have already several 
datasets for SLBs with 50% and 25% BMP at the presence of TAT, and I will continue to track the particles in those datasets and do MSD analysis to quantify the diffusion coefficient and confinement of the particles.
